Firstly, as this post is 7 years after Mr. Jordan's thread in the Pattern was cut, I suppose you are right in that he can't.  But reGARDless of his ability, the real question here is not whether he has the right to prohibit our expresson, but whether we can morally violate his wishes.  Yes, it is an honor to have fan fiction written.  If it was Mr. Jordan's express desire that it not be written, seems to me that would be enough to say, "let's not do this."  That is not to say that if you so chose to write fan fiction to be distributed to friends and relatives, or even as a school assignment, you couldn't do that - therein is our freedom of expression.   I would not, however, believe it right to post such things on public page - simply out of honoring a dead man's wish, which should be enough to stop us out of respect.
